description: Tier-0 public RAG smoke set derived from RFC 8259 for ingestion-to-evaluation canary coverage. It is not an external benchmark or a claim of retrieval-quality generalization.
purpose: Verify that ingestion, retrieval, answer generation, citation, and evaluation can execute on three public-source questions.

authoring_origin.basis: Questions and paraphrased references were prepared from RFC 8259 sections 6, 8.1, and 9.

answer_policy: Answer the question under one fixed policy. Use and cite retrieved contexts when supplied; without retrieved contexts, state that no retrieved evidence was supplied. If available information cannot support a requested value, say so.
citation_policy: With retrieval enabled, cite supporting passages inline as [context:N]. RAG-off answers must not invent retrieved citations.

test_cases.query: Does RFC 8259 permit Infinity, NaN, or leading zeros in JSON numbers?
test_cases.reference_answer: No. JSON number syntax excludes Infinity and NaN, and numbers cannot have leading zeros.

test_cases.query: What character encoding does RFC 8259 require between systems outside a closed ecosystem, and what are the byte order mark rules?
test_cases.reference_answer: Use UTF-8. Senders must not prefix network-transmitted JSON with a byte order mark. A receiving parser may ignore a mark that is present.

test_cases.query: Which implementation limits may a JSON parser set under RFC 8259 section 9?
test_cases.reference_answer: A parser may restrict input size, nesting depth, numeric range and precision, and string length and character contents.
